title: Check the emitted instruction variant before changing a GPU architecture gate
applies_when: A CUDA/Triton feature appears unsupported on a GPU family, especially Tensor Descriptor gather4 on sm120, or a hardware profile is being reused to admit an operator path.
lesson: Bind the exact PTX version, target and instruction qualifiers before inferring support from an architecture name. PTX9.3 distinguishes gather4 with shared::cta destination (sm100 or higher) from shared::cluster destination (restricted architecture/family targets). A cluster-form rejection therefore does not prove that every gather4 form fails on RTX5090/sm120. Inspect the actual generated PTX from the target compiler, prove the selected branch is reached and compare a bounded real numerical workload with its pointer/reference path before changing a capability guard. Keep the ISA fact separate from compiler lowering and measured operator behavior.
avoid_when: Do not transfer this statement to other PTX revisions, destination scopes, multicast/tcgen05 instructions or compiler versions without checking their own constraints. Compilation or a few numerical cases do not establish all-shape support, model accuracy, speedup or a performance ceiling. Do not change a correct gate merely because another kernel emitted an unsupported variant.

evidence.note: PTX9.3 Target ISA Notes give different target constraints for shared::cta and shared::cluster forms of tile::gather4.

Pinned upstream forced-config/modular WNA16 tests compare TD with pointer and Torch reference, assert actual USE_TD launch flags and include a single-token fallback. A future reproduction still needs a matching native environment and hardware.
